root.claim: One deterministic fixed-alphabet multitape Turing machine computes $\operatorname{bin}_{2n}(\operatorname{val}(x)\operatorname{val}(y))$ for all $n$-bit inputs in time $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ with $\kappa=2^{-182}$, refuting the $n\log n$ optimality conjecture in that model.
root.method: build two sub-logarithmic tape procedures (address-chunk interchange and simultaneous butterfly layers) from finite linear networks with a rank saving, insert them into the Harvey--van der Hoeven reduction of multiplication to convolution over $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ via a Chinese-remainder map, Gaussian resampling, chirps and a phase twist, recover the integer coefficients exactly, and sum the normalized cost table

motivation.text: In the $O(n\log n)$ approach every one of $\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels rescans $\Theta(n)$ bits, so going below $n\log n$ requires saving both on address movement and on butterfly arithmetic, which is what the two network-based procedures provide.

quote.quote:
Scanning an array of $\Theta(n)$ stored bits at each of
$\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$.
We therefore need savings in both movement and arithmetic.

children.claim: Two disjoint contiguous address fields of $u$ bits in an array of logical volume $V$ can be interchanged on a fixed number of tapes in $O(Vu^\tau)$ time for a fixed $\tau<1$.
children.method: run the bit network on row-split role streams, with frames given by rational address shears so that every edge is a few smaller interchanges, solve the volume-normalized recurrence at power widths, then remove the width and row restrictions

motivation.text: An interchange whose field width grows cannot be done by a bounded number of scans; the network turns one shear of width $mf$ into $s$ shears of width $f$ on streams of volume $V/W$, and since $s<Wm$ the recurrence saves a power of the width.

quote.quote:
Because the sum of these ranks is less than the number of wires times
$m$, the resulting recurrence saves a power of the chunk width.

children.claim: For a fixed radix, permuting two digit positions, moving one digit, splitting and merging on a digit with a pointwise map, and cyclically splitting whole rows into a fixed number of streams each take $O(V)$ steps.

quote.quote:
Each of the following operations on an array of
volume $V$ takes $O(V)$ steps on a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes:

children.claim: An address field $y\in[Q]$ placed after its control fields can be updated by $y\mapsto y+a(\text{controls})\bmod Q$, or scaled by a fixed rational unit, in $O(V)$ time.

quote.quote:
An update
\[
 y\longmapsto y+a(\text{controls})\pmod Q
\]
costs $O(V)$ if the offset can be prepared in $b^{O(1)}$ time from the
fixed number of control values.

children.claim: A fixed linear network of $W$ wires, built from three stages of invocations on $3$-element subsets of a $100$-element set, maps two data banks $(X,Y)$ to $(-Y,X)$ (a plain swap over $\mathbb F_2$) and restores every auxiliary wire whatever its initial value.
children.method: compose three stage invocations (forward, inverse, forward), each a restored eight-row schedule whose gather, scatter and side injections add $x_S$ to $y_S$

motivation.text: Each invocation only adds one bank to the other along a single tensor coordinate, so three alternating additions $X\to Y$, $Y\to X$, $X\to Y$ produce the signed exchange, as in the classical three-XOR swap, while the restoration schedule removes any dependence on scratch contents.

children.claim: The eight-row schedule changes the target bank by $(\mathcal J\mathcal V+\mathcal R\mathcal G)x$, independently of the arbitrary initial side and central scratch values.

quote.quote:
The net target change is
$(\mathcal J\mathcal V+\mathcal R\mathcal G)x$, independently of
$a,c$.

children.claim: Gather and scatter through central wires give coefficient $|S\cap T|\bmod 2$ (bit case) or $(|S\cap T|-1)/2$ (complex case) from $x_T$ to $y_S$, and the side wires cancel the unwanted neighbors, so each invocation performs $y_S\gets y_S+x_S$.

quote.quote:
In the complex case, the central coefficient is $(|S\cap T|-1)/2$.
The side cancels it for distinct triples with intersection zero or two;
intersection one contributes zero, and the self coefficient is one.
Thus both net maps are $y\gets y+x$.

children.claim: Applying $Y\gets Y+X$, then $X\gets X-Y$, then $Y\gets Y+X$ sends $(x,y)$ to $(-y,x)$.

quote.quote:
The inverse schedule with logical source $Y$ and target $X$ effects
$X\gets X-Y$.  Starting from $(x,y)$, the three stages give
$(x,y+x)$, then $(-y,y+x)$, then $(-y,x)$.

children.salient: The final effect is an exact permutation of the data banks even though intermediate wires carry XOR or linear combinations of data, and it holds for arbitrary initial scratch values.

children.claim: If every vertex $v$ of the network carries an invertible frame $D_v$ shared by all wires at a gate, and each edge applies $D_vD_u^{-1}$, the network on arrays implements $D_{\rm out}\mathsf S_\Omega D_{\rm in}^{-1}$, so only the endpoint frames matter.

quote.quote:
Thus the common frame commutes with the pointwise gate, and
the invariant continues to the sinks.

children.claim: Nondegenerate subspaces of the $m$-dimensional space $F^{\otimes 3}$ can be attached to the terminals and gates so that labels on every edge are nested, the only decreasing edges are the central-wire returns, and the absolute dimension changes sum to $Wm-2N+2L$ with $L<N/2$.

quote.quote:
Every edge joins comparable nondegenerate labels.  The only decreasing
edges are the central-wire edges from time 3 to time 4; their dimension
loss is $h$.

children.claim: For both networks the total number $s$ of smaller calls (rational edge ranks for the bit network, residual dimensions for the complex one) satisfies $s<Wm$, and in fact $s/W<m^\tau$ with $\tau=1-2^{-50}$.

quote.quote:
Consequently
\[
 \frac{s_{\rm b}}{W_{\rm b}}<m^\tau,
 \qquad \frac{s_{\rm c}}{W_{\rm c}}<m^\sigma,

children.salient: The inequality $s<Wm$ is strict, with loss ratios $L/N=100/539$ and $101/539$ both below $1/2$; this strict deficit is the entire source of the power saving.

children.claim: For widths $e=m^k$ with a row field divisible by $W^k$, two chunks of $e$ digits can be interchanged in $O(Ve^\tau)$ time.
children.method: implement the shear $H\gets H+D$ by the bit network on $W$ row-split role streams with frames $\Phi_M$, realize each edge matrix of rank $a$ by $a$ smaller interchanges, finish with two linear-cost updates, and solve $F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$

motivation.text: Dividing cost by volume, each level multiplies the recursive contribution by $s/W$, which is less than the factor $m$ by which the width grows, so the geometric sum gives a power below one.

quote.quote:
After dividing cost by volume, multiplying the parameter by $m$
increases the recursive contribution by $s/W<m$. This strict inequality
is the source of the power saving.

children.claim: Every rational $m\times m$ matrix of rank $a$ factors as $E_1\Pi E_2$ with $E_1,E_2$ invertible lower triangular and $\Pi$ a partial permutation with exactly $a$ ones.

quote.quote:
Every rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$ has a factorization
\[
 A=E_1\Pi E_2,
\]

children.claim: The address shear $(H,D)\mapsto(H+AD,D)$ by a fixed rational matrix of rank $a$ needs exactly $a$ interchanges of $b$-digit fields plus $O(V)$ further work.

quote.quote:
can be performed with exactly $a$ interchanges of pairs of $b$-digit
fields and $O(V)$ further work.

children.claim: Distributing whole rows cyclically among the $W$ wire roles gives role streams with a common address set, each of volume $V/W$, on which gates act pointwise.

quote.quote:
Split whole rows cyclically into $W$ role streams within each prefix
preceding the row field.

children.claim: With frames $\Phi_{M_v}$ and endpoint identity $M_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}-M_{\mathrm{source}(w)}=I_m$, the network applies the shear $H\gets H+D$ on every role, and two further linear-cost updates turn it into the interchange $(H,D)\mapsto(D,H)$.

quote.quote:
The result
is $H\leftarrow H+D$ on every original row, including rows assigned
to scratch roles, whose initial values were arbitrary.

children.claim: The $s$ recursive calls each act on volume $V/W$, so $F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$, and $s/W<m^\tau$ gives $F_k=O(e^\tau)$.

quote.quote:
For $a=s/W<m^\tau$ the geometric sum
$\sum_{j=0}^k a^j$ is $O(m^{k\tau})$.

children.claim: Parking the $W-1$ inactive role streams on a stack tape lets one fixed set of tapes serve every recursion depth with overhead $O(V)$ per node.

quote.quote:
Each push, pop, copy, positioning operation, or erasure moves $O(V)$
symbols at a parent node.

children.claim: Arbitrary widths $u$ are handled by taking rows from a few high digits, padding to a multiple of $W^k$, splitting the width in base $m$ into power-width pieces, and padding binary ranges to powers of the prime $q$, all within $O(Vu^\tau)$.

quote.quote: Rows for a general array can be supplied by a few of its own high digits.

children.salient: The procedure's final effect is a pure permutation of data, yet it beats the cost of moving fields digit by digit only because it computes XOR combinations of data along the way.

adds.name: field width
adds.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two address fields being interchanged.

children.claim: A layer of normalized butterflies $H_0$ on the same bit position of $D\le d$ address chunks of an array of polynomial records can be applied, exactly and then truncated once, in $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ time for a fixed $\lambda'<1$.
children.method: write the $H_0$ layer as $b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D$, compute $C^{\otimes e}$ by the complex network with binary phase frames (each edge is a few $C$ layers on $e/m$ chunks after packed binary basis changes), recurse on row-split streams, keep exact Gaussian dyadics with guard bits and truncate once

motivation.text: Applying $D$ butterfly factors one after another costs $D$ whole-array passes; the phase frames express a $C$ tensor product through smaller groups of selected bits so that the rank saving $s<Wm$ gives a sublinear dependence on $d$.

quote.quote:
We will obtain cost $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$, with
$\lambda'<1$ and $V$ the logical bit volume, whereas separate butterfly
factors would require $D$ whole-array passes.

children.claim: The kernel $C=H\mathsf SH=aI+bX$ with $a=(1+i)/2$, $b=(1-i)/2$ satisfies $H_0=b\mathsf SC\mathsf S$, $C^4=I$ and $C^{-1}=-iZCZ$, all with Gaussian dyadic coefficients.

With binary phase frames $\mathcal C_U$ on the complex network, each edge factors into one translation kernel per orthonormal residual vector, so a group of $e=mf$ selected axes needs exactly $s$ child calls on $f$ axes, after binary basis changes, and the endpoints give $C^{\otimes e}$ on every role.

quote.quote:
Summing its residual dimensions gives exactly
$s_{\rm c}$ child calls, each on the $f=e/m$ axes of one slot.

children.claim: On all $D$ selected coordinates, $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D$, where $\mathcal S_D$ is a diagonal fourth-root phase and $b^D$ a binary shift and phase.

quote.quote:
Applying
\eqref{eq:phase-basic-identities} on all selected coordinates gives

children.claim: A binary row addition on selected bits of two address chunks is performed by eight packed cyclic shifts of whole chunk ranges plus a deterministic sort-based repair of a small exceptional set, in $O(V(L^\tau+1))$ time for chunks of $L$ bits.

quote.quote:
The construction first uses a constant number
of cyclic shifts of whole chunk ranges, then corrects an explicitly bounded set of
addresses.

children.claim: Splitting rows among the $W$ roles gives the time-per-volume recurrence $F(e)\le(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^\tau+1)$, which unrolls to $O(d^{\lambda'})$.

quote.quote:
Indeed, the \(s\) child calls are executed on streams of volume
\(V/W\), so their total cost is \(s(V/W)F(e/m)\).

children.claim: Reserving $p+\Delta$ fractional and $\Delta+3$ integer bits, with $\Delta=\lceil C_0d^{C_1}\rceil=o(p)$, represents every intermediate value of the layer exactly.

quote.quote:
Thus reserving \(p+\Delta\)
fractional bits and \(\Delta+3\) integer and sign bits per real
component represents every intermediate coefficient exactly and
prevents overflow.

children.claim: Since $H_0^{\otimes D}$ maps disk arrays to disk arrays, the single final truncation $Q_p$ keeps the output in the disk with error below $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$.

quote.quote:
Finally, every row of $\mathcal H$ has
absolute row sum one.

children.claim: Normalized cyclic convolution of arrays of $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ records on power-of-two axes of total size $T$ can be approximated within $\sqrt2\,M(3\ell+1)2^{-p}$ at cost $O(Tp[dK+pK^{\tau-1}+\ell d^{\lambda'}+\log(rp)])$.
children.method: compute two forward synthetic transforms on a layout where each round is one simultaneous butterfly layer, keep their stored frequency order through packed pointwise polynomial products, and apply one opposite transform

motivation.text: In the ring $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ the roots of unity needed by the transform are powers of $y$, which act by signed shifts, so the transform reduces to butterfly layers and address moves, the two operations made fast above.

quote.quote:
Their entries will be short polynomials in a quotient
where the required roots of unity act by exact signed permutations
of coefficient lists.

children.claim: The decimation-in-frequency recursion with synthetic roots $\omega_t=y^{2r/t}$ computes $B_tF_t^-$ (frequency $j$ stored at slot $\operatorname{rev}(j)$), and the reversed recursion computes $F_t^+B_t^{-1}$.

quote.quote:
If
$\operatorname{rev}_a(j)$ reverses the $a$ binary digits of $j$, the
entry $(F_t^-z)_j$ occupies slot $\operatorname{rev}_a(j)$.

children.claim: A layout permutation $L$ puts the bits of all axes at common offsets in consecutive $K$-bit chunks, so each round is one simultaneous layer plus a recordwise twiddle shift, giving the multidimensional transform with error below $\sqrt2\ell\,2^{-p}$ at cost $O(Tp[dK+pK^{\tau-1}+\ell d^{\lambda'}])$.

quote.quote:
The procedure constructs an explicit positional
layout permutation $L$ of record addresses, preserving their polynomial
suffixes, and transforms disk grid arrays of $M$ contiguous
degree-less-than-$r$ polynomial records.

children.claim: Pointwise products commute with the common record permutation $LB$, so the forward outputs can be multiplied in their stored order and passed directly to the opposite transform.

quote.quote:
Pointwise multiplication commutes with applying the same record
permutation $LB$ to both operands.

children.claim: Each pointwise product $Q_p(fg/r)$ in $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ is computed exactly by signed Kronecker substitution with four calls to the established multiplier, in $O(rp\log(rp))$ time.

quote.quote:
One can compute the exact Gaussian integer
numerators of $fg$, and then return $Q_p(fg/r)$ in that same format, in time
$O(rp\log(rp))$ on a fixed number of tapes.

children.claim: Since all exact steps are contractions, the errors of the three transforms and the product add, and the final exact scaling by $M$ gives total error below $\sqrt2\,M(3\ell+1)2^{-p}$.

quote.quote:
The final exact multiplication by $M$ therefore gives error less than
$M(3\delta+\eta)=\sqrt2\,M(3\ell+1)2^{-p}$, as claimed.

children.claim: The permuted multidimensional source transform $RF_{\boldsymbol s}$ on distinct prime axes equals $2^\gamma\mathcal B_0QF_{\boldsymbol t}\mathcal A$ with power-of-two axes, its middle factor $QF_{\boldsymbol t}$ is a chirp-wrapped cyclic convolution, and the retained permutation $R$ cancels in a convolution.
children.method: apply Gaussian resampling linewise while keeping the source and target permutations inside the identity, evaluate the middle factor by Bluestein's chirp identity, and show the source permutation cancels

motivation.text: The prime lengths needed for the integer product do not match the power-of-two lengths of the synthetic transforms; resampling bridges them, and leaving the permutations in the formula avoids two sorts per coordinate.

quote.quote:
The transform lengths needed for the integer product are pairwise coprime,
whereas the synthetic transforms use powers of two. Gaussian resampling
connects these two shapes.

children.claim: For coprime $s<t$ with enough separation, $P_sF_s=2^{2\alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA$ for contractions $A,B_0$ built from Gaussian kernels, approximable with error below $p^2$ in $O(tp^{3/2+\delta}\alpha)$ time.

quote.quote:
There are linear contractions $A:\mathbb C^s\to\mathbb C^t$ and
$B_0:\mathbb C^t\to\mathbb C^s$ satisfying

children.claim: Applying the one-dimensional maps line by line gives the tensor identity $RF_{\boldsymbol s}=2^\gamma\mathcal B_0QF_{\boldsymbol t}\mathcal A$, with axis movements done by chunk interchanges.

quote.quote:
For the tensor product, apply the one-dimensional maps to one coordinate
line at a time.

children.claim: With the chirp $a_{\boldsymbol j}=\exp(-\pi i\sum_i s_ij_i^2/t_i)$, $QF_{\boldsymbol t}u=\overline a\cdot(a*(\overline a\cdot u))/T$, so the target permutation is absorbed by the chirp.

quote.quote:
The factor $QF_{\boldsymbol t}$ in \eqref{eq:no-sort-tensor} can be
computed from a cyclic convolution and two pointwise phase
multiplications.

children.claim: $(RF_{\boldsymbol s}^+)[(RF_{\boldsymbol s}u)\cdot(RF_{\boldsymbol s}v)]=(u*v)/S^2$, so the source permutation $R$ never has to be executed.

quote.quote:
The second identity shows how the
retained source permutation $R$ cancels when computing a convolution.

adds.name: source permutation
adds.meaning: The coordinate permutation on the prime source axes that Gaussian resampling leaves in the transform identity.

adds.name: target permutation
adds.meaning: The coordinate permutation on the power-of-two axes that Gaussian resampling leaves in the transform identity.

adds.name: resampling scale exponent
adds.meaning: The exponent $2d\alpha^2$ of the power-of-two scale factor in the tensor resampling identity.

children.claim: Distinct odd primes $s_i$ with $(1-2\eta)t_i<s_i\le(1-\eta)t_i$ exist, give $T/2<S<T$, and satisfy every hypothesis of the resampling lemma for large $n$.

quote.quote:
Thus every hypothesis of Lemma~\ref{lem:no-sort-resampling} holds for
all sufficiently large input lengths.

children.claim: Splitting the inputs into $q=\lceil n/b\rceil$ radix-$2^b$ digits makes the product a convolution of coefficients $0\le c_j<2^{3b}$, with no wraparound modulo $x^S-1$.

quote.quote: Thus convolution modulo $x^S-1$ has no nonzero wraparound.

children.claim: The map $x\mapsto\prod_ix_i^{\mu_i}$ is an isomorphism from cyclic convolution of length $S$ to multidimensional cyclic convolution on the prime axes, implemented by triangular controlled shifts and axis moves in $O(Tp\,d^2(1+\ell^\tau))$ time.

quote.quote:
Hence
$\Phi$ is an isomorphism and preserves cyclic convolution.

children.claim: Multiplying coefficient $k$ of the last axis by $\zeta^k$, $\zeta=e^{\pi i/r}$, turns normalized complex cyclic convolution on power-of-two axes into convolution over $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$, and untwisting recovers the cyclic wrap with the correct sign.

quote.quote:
Untwisting therefore recovers the cyclic coefficient with the correct
sign.

children.claim: The composed procedure (CRT map, two source transforms, pointwise product, opposite transform, rescaling) returns every product coefficient within less than $1/2$, so rounding and carry propagation give exactly $\operatorname{bin}_{2n}(\operatorname{val}(x)\operatorname{val}(y))$.
children.method: identify the exact counterpart of the computed pipeline as the integer convolution, add the contraction errors of all stages, bound the final error below $1/2$, round, and propagate carries

motivation.text: The true coefficients are integers, so any approximation with error below $1/2$ determines them by rounding, and carries then give the binary product; since every stage is a contraction, the errors can simply be summed.

children.claim: By the permutation cancellation, the exact counterpart after the three transforms is $(u*v)/S^2$, and the two scalings by $S$ and $2^{2b+4}$ recover the integer coefficient convolution.

quote.quote:
By \eqref{eq:source-permutation-cancel}, the exact
counterpart after the three transforms is $(u*v)/S^2$, so after the
first scale it is $w=(u*v)/S$.

children.claim: For contractions errors propagate without growth, and for bilinear contractions on disk operands the two input errors add.

quote.quote: When all four operands are in the disk, their two errors therefore add.

children.claim: The final absolute error is below $448b\,2^{-3b/4}<1/2$, so rounding gives the unique correct integer coefficient.

quote.quote:
The strict error below $1/2$ makes the nearest integer to
that value the unique correct coefficient.

children.claim: Propagating radix-$2^b$ carries in increasing coefficient order yields the exact binary product.

quote.quote:
The unprocessed terms are multiples of $Q_0^j$, so the identity fixes
the first $j$ radix digits of the full product.

children.claim: With $\tau=1-2^{-50}$, $\lambda'=1-2^{-54}$, $c=2^{-56}$, $\epsilon=2^{-75}$ and $V=Tp=\Theta(n)$, every normalized cost term is at most $p^{1-2\kappa}$, so the total time is $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ for large $n$.

quote.quote:
Each of the seven displayed powers is at most $1-2\kappa$ by
\eqref{eq:margin-list}.

children.salient: The smallest margin is $g_2=\epsilon c(1-\tau)=2^{-181}=2\kappa$, coming from the chunk exchanges of the transform layout, which is why $\kappa$ is as tiny as $2^{-182}$.

children.claim: Below one fixed cutoff the machine uses schoolbook multiplication, so the bound holds for every $n\ge1$.

quote.quote:
Fix one cutoff beyond all the size, precision, margin and layout
conditions, and use schoolbook multiplication below it.

children.claim: A single machine with time $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ has $T_A(n)/(n\lg n)\to0$, which refutes an eventual $\Omega(n\lg n)$ lower bound in the fixed multitape model.

quote.quote:
The theorem refutes an
eventual $\Omega(n\log n)$ lower bound for every fixed multiplication
machine in this model.

root.salient: The saving is a fixed power of the logarithm, uniform over all input lengths, with the explicit but tiny exponent $\kappa=2^{-182}$.

adds.name: logical volume
adds.meaning: The number of stored data bits of the array an operation acts on.

adds.name: wire count
adds.meaning: The number of wires, including scratch wires, of the fixed linear network in use.

adds.name: label dimension
adds.meaning: The dimension $h^3=10^6$ of the bilinear space whose subspaces label the network.

adds.name: smaller-call count
adds.meaning: The total number of smaller recursive calls one network invocation makes, summed over its edges.

adds.name: working precision
adds.meaning: The number of fractional bits of the fixed-point coefficient grid $2^{-p}\mathbb Z[i]$.

adds.name: axis count
adds.meaning: The number of transform axes, which bounds the number of chunks a butterfly layer acts on.

adds.name: record length
adds.meaning: The number of complex coefficients of each polynomial record in $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$.

adds.name: padded box size
adds.meaning: The number of complex entries in the padded power-of-two box, the product of the axis lengths.

adds.name: source size
adds.meaning: The product of the distinct prime source axis lengths, the length of the cyclic convolution.

adds.name: interchange exponent
adds.meaning: The fixed exponent $1-2^{-50}$ below one in the address-interchange cost bound.

adds.name: layer exponent
adds.meaning: The fixed exponent below one in the simultaneous butterfly layer cost bound.
